**Tier 5** — results — pinned to dataset + policy + engine version · owned by `engine` · `public.run_replications`

**One row is** One replication of one simulation run: the seed it used, the KPI row the engine computed for it, and its weekly series. A run has as many rows here as it has replications, and `rep_index` orders them. Tier 5 — a RESULT, derived from a tier-2 dataset by a named engine version, never an input to anything. Nothing downstream reads it except the result surfaces; a row is superseded by re-running, never edited.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `run_replications_pkey` |
| `run_id` + `rep_index` | UNIQUE index | `rep_run_index_uq` |
| `run_id` + `rep_index` | UNIQUE index | `run_replications_run_rep_uniq` |

**Natural key:** `run_id` + `rep_index` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `rep_run_index_uq`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `simulation_lab` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — **2 with no predicate** |

`write: simulation_lab` is the capability that gates the only user-facing action which writes this table — running a simulation. It is NOT `null`, and the first draft of this sidecar said it was: `analysis_runs` can claim `write: null` because it has no write policy at all and every write goes through a SECURITY DEFINER RPC, but this table is written by the BROWSER, as a PostgREST upsert from `pyodideEngine.persistEngineResult`, behind two predicate-less policies (`rep_auth_all` and `run_replications_anon_write`). `governanceEnforcement.test.ts` refused the `null` claim on exactly that evidence, and it was right: a policy with no predicate permits any holder of the table grant to write, which is a user-facing write path whether or not a page uses it. So the capability is declared and the exposure is stated rather than implied: this is one of the eleven tables §4 D154 measured as genuinely writable from the browser's `anon` role. That is D28's standing decision (document, do not change) and WP 7.1's to close — `min_project_role` is `viewer` because nothing here enforces a role today, not because a viewer ought to be able to write results. NOT AUDITED, and that is the tier rather than an omission: the audit rule (`audit-actor`) covers tiers 2, 3 and 4, where a write changes the world a later run will see. A replication row is the OUTPUT of one run and an input to nothing; re-running writes new rows rather than mutating these, so there is no tier transition here for an audit row to name.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 2 policies here grant access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `rep_auth_all` — `ALL` to `authenticated`
> - `run_replications_anon_write` — `ALL` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> Some of these permit **writes**. See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

### `kpis`

This replication's KPI row, exactly as `compute_replication_kpis` built it: fill rate, revenue, lost sales, peak backlog, the inventory window averages, capacity utilization and one `cost_<component>` key per entry of scsim's COST_COMPONENTS. Units are per-key and follow the engine's definition of each measure, which is why `unit_source` is `derived` rather than a single token.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `jsonb`, `NOT NULL`, default `'{}'::jsonb` |
| Grain | `level` |
| Unit | none recorded (derived) |
| Added by | `20260607121406_fcbd47e9-93de-4b3b-988f-7f4718159c91.sql` |
| Read by the engine | `scsim_bridge.py::compute_run_from_project -> replications[].kpis` |
| Transform | _finite(v, 6) per key — NaN and ±inf become null, which is valid JSON |
| Validated at ingest | — |
| Rendered at | *not yet recorded (WP 5.1)* |

> The KEYS are a vocabulary this file does not restate — they are the engine's, and `deriveRunKpis` reads them from it so the manual cannot drift from what a run carries. §4 D113 is what restating them costs: a display list built from the LEGACY engine's KPI shape offered eleven rows the canonical engine never writes. NO `computed_by`: its contract is a writer `contract:check` R18 can find in `src/` or `supabase/functions/`, and the producer here is Python (`scsim/scsim/kpi/compute.py::compute_replication_kpis`) running in Pyodide. Naming it there would be a declaration R18 cannot resolve — §4 D118's shape. `engine.consumed_by` carries the path instead.

### `time_series`

This replication's weekly series, one array per key, each as long as the horizon in weeks. The keys are scsim's PUBLISHED weekly series and are declared in ONE place — `WEEKLY_SERIES` in scsim/scsim/core/context.py — which also fixes each series' unit and how it may be aggregated across weeks (`level` = a stock, average it; `flow` = a weekly quantity, sum it; `ratio` = neither). `unit_source` is `derived` because the unit is per-key, from that declaration, not one token for the column. The four inventory series (`on_hand_value`, `fg_value`, `on_hand_units`, `fg_units`) are what WP 9.1 added to a user's view; `fg_value` had been computed on every replication since the trace was written and published by nothing, because the vocabulary was authored six times and it was present in only two of them (§4 D164).

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `jsonb`, `NOT NULL`, default `'{}'::jsonb` |
| Grain | `level` |
| Unit | none recorded (derived) |
| Added by | `20260607121406_fcbd47e9-93de-4b3b-988f-7f4718159c91.sql` |
| Read by the engine | `scsim_bridge.py::compute_run_from_project -> replications[].time_series` |
| Transform | fill_rate from fr_series, every other published series iterated generically out of extra_series; _finite(x, 5) per element |
| Validated at ingest | — |
| Rendered at | *not yet recorded (WP 5.1)* |

> Rendered on BOTH result surfaces — `InventoryOverTime` (materials and finished goods, units or value), `WeeklySeriesChart` and `ReplicationSeedExplorer` — all fed by the hook's `select *` cited at table grain, so there is no column-grain read to cite. A run made before a series existed carries a row WITHOUT that key. The inventory panel states that rather than drawing a zero line, because a missing measurement and a measured zero are different facts and T1 does not allow one to stand in for the other. NO `computed_by`, for the reason given on `kpis`: the producer is scsim, which R18 cannot resolve. `engine.consumed_by` carries the path.
